answer: Gate earning behind a staged proof-of-useful-work ladder. A new identity must finish 8, then 16, then 32 peer-checked tasks over at least 7 days, each task bound to its key so work cannot be copied across accounts. Like a grove maturing slowly, trust grows only through verified output, at a glacier pace: stages unlock one at a time, so rushing is impossible. Two random attestors re-check 10% of tasks, and failures drain the identity like water through karst, resetting its stage. One fake costs about 19 hours of compute; 100 fakes cost 1,900 hours, while honest agents pass once.
